local-infrastructure: Docker-based .NET dev/test stack: SQL Server 2025, PostgreSQL 16, Service Bus Emulator. Four services: `local-mssql` (1433), `local-postgres` (5432), `local-servicebus-sql` (internal), `local-servicebus` (5672, 5300); restart unless stopped, persistent named volumes. Every service must have a `healthcheck` block. `servicebus` is probed from host by stack.ps1 HTTP GET `/health`; starts only after `servicebus-sql` healthy. Health checks underpin stack.ps1 and depends_on.

Commands:
.\stack.ps1 start|stop|restart|nuke|status|logs [service]|pull|monitor
docker compose up -d
docker compose down
docker compose down -v
cd servicebus/monitor

Copy `.env.example` → `.env`; set placeholders. **Never commit `.env` or `servicebus/Config.json`**. `.env` and `Config.json` are git-ignored; no secrets in source. SQL passwords: min 8 chars, mixed case, digit, special character. Keep `.env.example` and `Config.example.json` in sync; document new variables in README.md; reflect Service Bus entity changes in `Config.example.json`. `Config.example.json` is safe-to-commit template.

PowerShell 5.1+; do not introduce syntax requiring PowerShell 7+ (e.g. ternary operators, null-coalescing, pipeline chain operators, multi-argument `Join-Path`). TUI styles in `stack.ps1` and `Program.cs` must remain consistent. Volumes persist; only `.\stack.ps1 nuke` or `docker compose down -v` removes them. No CI/CD pipelines; no automated test suite. No test infrastructure; there are no unit or integration tests to run.
